item.title: What a Year! LPi’s Top Moments of 2025
item.description: Here are just a few standout moments that reflect the passion and dedication of our teams — and what made 2025 a year to remember!

item.title: The Carpenter and the Law | Sixth Sunday in Ordinary Time
item.description: My husband and I couldn’t believe our luck: our new house had a deck. It was more than a couple of broke millennials had ever dared to dream about. We had arrived.

item.title: When we go Into the Desert | First Sunday of Lent
item.description: When we first got married, I wanted to know everything my husband was thinking, exactly when he was thinking it. Thirteen years later, I still want to know it all.

item.title: 76 Church Event Ideas Your Parishioners Will Love
item.description: Church events that work: 75 creative, fun, and seasonal ideas for every parish and every age group.

item.title: Build Three Tents | The Second Sunday of Lent
item.description: When I went to Indianapolis in the summer of 2024 to cover the NEC for our archdiocesan newspaper, I knew it would be a fun and spiritually rich experience.

item.title: When God asks for Water | Third Sunday of Lent
item.description: This was when I learned that it feels good to help people, and this memory is a perpetually replenished well of living water for me.

item.title: How Successful Churches Use Canva for Parish Bulletins and More
item.description: Thousands of churches have leveled-up the design part of their communications thanks to Canva. Learn how your parish can, too!

item.title: We
item.description: Nowhere in the Gospel story does it say that Jesus promised the man sight if he washed in the pool. I wonder what it was that made him feel he could trust Jesus.

item.title: Where to Find Professional Virgin Mary Images for Catholic Parish
item.description: How and where to find the BEST graphics of Mary to use for your church without worrying about copyright!

item.title: What Lazarus Wanted | The Fifth Sunday of Lent
item.description: “It must be so crazy, being God,” one of my friends said. “Does it feel like playing The Sims? Just making people do stuff because you want to see what happens?”
